questions.question_text: On 26 August 2019, applying the Bimal Jalan Committee's framework, RBI's Central Board decided to keep realised equity at 5.5% of the balance sheet (the lower bound of the Contingent Risk Buffer range of 5.5%–6.5%). The 2018-19 net income was ₹1,23,414 crore and excess risk provisions of ₹52,637 crore were written back. What was the total transfer to the Government, and why was there an excess?

options.text: ₹1,23,414 crore; the excess provisions were retained as a buffer
₹1,76,051 crore; realised equity stood at 6.8% of the balance sheet, above the chosen 5.5% level
₹1,76,051 crore; realised equity had fallen below 5.5%, so provisions were released
₹70,777 crore; the excess was deducted from the year's surplus

solution.concept: Surplus distribution under the revised Economic Capital Framework
solution.explanation: Available realised equity was 6.8% of the balance sheet. Keeping it at the lower bound of 5.5% released excess provisions of ₹52,637 crore, written back. The entire net income of ₹1,23,414 crore was also transferable, so the transfer was 1,23,414 + 52,637 = ₹1,76,051 crore.
steps: Realised equity 6.8% > chosen 5.5% → excess ₹52,637 crore written back
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹1,23,414 crore omits the write-back; realised equity was above, not below, the range; ₹70,777 crore subtracts instead of adding.
solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹1,76,051 crore; realised equity stood at 6.8% of the balance sheet, above the chosen 5.5% level

fact_checks.claim: decided to transfer a sum of ₹1,76,051 crore to the Government of India comprising of ₹1,23,414 crore of surplus for the year 2018-19 and ₹52,637 crore of excess provisions

solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following definitions given in RBI's currency FAQs:
I. A 'soiled note' includes a two-piece note pasted together where both pieces belong to the same note and form the entire note with no essential feature missing.
II. A 'mutilated banknote' is one of which a portion is missing or which is composed of more than two pieces.
III. An 'imperfect banknote' is one that is obliterated, shrunk, washed, altered or indecipherable, and includes a mutilated note.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: A soiled note includes a two-piece note pasted together with both pieces of the same note and no essential feature missing (I). A mutilated note has a portion missing or more than two pieces (II). An imperfect note is wholly or partially obliterated, shrunk, washed, altered or indecipherable but does NOT include a mutilated note, so III is wrong.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: A 'soiled note' means a note which has become dirty due to normal wear and tear and includes a two-piece note pasted together wherein both the pieces presented belong to the same note and form the entire note with no essential feature missing

'Mutilated banknote' is a banknote, of which a portion is missing, or which is composed of more than two pieces. 'Imperfect banknote' means any banknote, which is wholly or partially, obliterated, shrunk, washed, altered or indecipherable but does not include a mutilated banknote

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In the Cheque Truncation System, what does 'cheque truncation' mean?

options.text: Stopping the flow of the physical cheque during clearing, once an electronic image is generated, at the presenting bank
Cancelling a cheque that has crossed its validity period
Converting a cheque into a demand draft
Returning a dishonoured cheque to the drawer

solution.explanation: Cheque truncation is the stopping of the physical cheque's flow in the clearing cycle as soon as an electronic image is generated for transmission. In India the presenting bank truncates the cheque, so physical instruments need not move across branches.
steps: Image generated → physical cheque stops at presenting bank
solution.why_others_wrong: Truncation has nothing to do with stale cheques, demand drafts or returns.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Stopping the flow of the physical cheque during clearing, once an electronic image is generated, at the presenting bank
